name: Video Poker
description: Video Poker is a casino card game played on machines (or digitally). Based on Five-Card Draw poker. Player gets 5 cards, chooses which to hold/discard, draws replacements. Payout based on final hand strength. Jacks or Better is most common variant. Perfect strategy yields near 99.5% return.
deck: Standard 52-card deck (+ jokers in some variants)

history.origins: Video poker first became commercially viable in the mid-1970s when it became economical to combine a television-like monitor with a solid-state CPU; the earliest models appeared alongside the first personal computers. SIRCOMA (Si Redd's Coin Machines, later International Game Technology) introduced Draw Poker in 1979. Throughout the 1980s video poker became increasingly popular in US casinos as players found the machines less intimidating than table games. The game has its roots in five-card draw but is played against a machine with a fixed paytable rather than against other hands.
timeline: 1970s: First video poker machines in USA.
1980s: Video poker spread widely in US casinos.
history.cultural: Worldwide casino game; especially popular with Las Vegas locals and in regulated online markets.
history.evolution: Became staple of casino gaming; multi-hand and online variants followed.

rules.objective: Achieve best poker hand. Higher hand = higher payout.
rules.gameplay: Bet coins. Receive 5 cards. Hold desired cards, discard rest. Draw replacements. Final hand evaluated against pay table. Jacks or Better: minimum pair of Jacks to win.

strategy.basic: Hold pairs. Keep high cards (J+). Never break a winning hand.
